beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit credentials to source control; provide a .env.example with placeholders only.
Require TLS/SSL on the MongoDB connection (e.g., use mongodb+srv or tls=true) and reject insecure connections; fail fast if TLS cannot be established.

Use a connection pool and sensible driver options: set maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, and enable retryWrites where supported; reuse one shared Mongoose/driver connection across the app and close it on shutdown.

Persist and use change stream resume tokens so the monitor can recover from restarts and transient errors without losing events; store the resume token outside memory (e.g., a small collection or durable store) after every processed event batch.
Keep heartbeat documents small and fixed-shape (e.g., {atmId, status, cashLevel, ts, geo}) and store large attachments or logs off-db (blob storage) to avoid large-document limits and RU spikes.
Create indexes that match read/query patterns: at minimum index atmId and ts (compound index {atmId:1, ts:-1}) for latest-heartbeat queries and index status for fast availability aggregation.

Maintain a single network summary document per monitored scope and update it atomically with update operators (e.g., updateOne with $inc, $set) or upsert, rather than recomputing from scratch on every change to reduce RU costs and race conditions.

Avoid multi-document transactions for high-throughput heartbeat writes; prefer single-document atomic updates or idempotent upserts for summary/alert state to minimize cross-partition transactions and RU consumption.

Use a TTL mechanism to expire old heartbeat documents to control storage growth (e.g., TTL index on ts) or implement a background prune job if TTL indexes are not available/compatible with the engine.
Instrument and monitor RU/s (or request units) and index usage; provision sufficient throughput or enable autoscale to handle ingestion spikes from many ATMs sending frequent heartbeats.
Implement exponential backoff and jitter for transient network/429/5xx errors and integrate driver-level retryWrites when available; limit retry attempts to avoid overwhelming the server.
When using change streams, filter server-side with an aggregate pipeline ($match on fullDocument.atmId or status) to reduce event volume and RU/throughput costs.

Persist alert state (e.g., active alerts list, lastTriggeredAt) in the DB and de-duplicate alert notifications by using idempotent writes/conditional updates so transient flapping doesn't cause repeated alerts.

Use appropriate readPreference/readConcern for your consistency needs (e.g., majority/primary for correctness of status and summaries) but be aware of compatibility/latency tradeoffs on the managed service.
Model per-ATM state in a dedicated collection with a unique index on atmId to allow cheap lookups and fast updates for online/offline checks rather than scanning heartbeat history.

When building Mongoose schemas, set strict schemas, appropriate field types, and explicit indexes in the schema, and avoid Mongoose middleware that blocks high-throughput insert paths (prefer lightweight validation or pre-validation off the hot path).

For vector-capable clusters, create vector indexes with appropriate index type and parameters (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN and their index params) and test vector search latency and RU cost with representative vectors before enabling in production.
Do not log the full DOCUMENTDB_URI or any tokens; redact connection strings and only log non-sensitive connection status, error codes, and metrics for diagnostics.
